intent.raw_query: Costa Rica eco-adventure, $2500, zip-lining and wildlife, February 2026 from Miami

experiences.name: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour
experiences.description: Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most thrilling zip-line circuits, featuring over 10 cables, Tarzan swings, and suspension bridges. Spot howler monkeys, toucans, and resplendent quetzals from a bird's-eye view while gliding above the treetops at speeds up to 50 mph.

experiences.name: Tortuguero National Park Wildlife Boat Safari
experiences.description: Glide through the jungle canals of Tortuguero on a guided boat safari teeming with wildlife. Observe caimans, river turtles, three-toed sloths, poison dart frogs, and over 300 bird species in their natural habitat. If visiting between July and October, witness the awe-inspiring nesting of endangered green sea turtles on the beach at night.

experiences.name: Manuel Antonio National Park Guided Eco-Hike
experiences.description: Explore Costa Rica's most biodiverse national park with a certified naturalist guide who will help you spot white-faced capuchin monkeys, two-toed sloths, scarlet macaws, and the rare squirrel monkey. The hike winds through lush rainforest trails that open onto stunning white-sand beaches, offering a perfect blend of wildlife and natural beauty.

experiences.name: Arenal Volcano Hanging Bridges & Hot Springs Evening
experiences.description: Walk among the rainforest canopy on a series of hanging bridges near the iconic Arenal Volcano, spotting poison dart frogs, leaf-cutter ants, and exotic birds. Cap the adventure with a relaxing soak in natural volcanic hot springs surrounded by lush jungle, a perfect recovery after days of eco-adventure activities.
experiences.location: La Fortuna de San Carlos, Alajuela Province

experiences.name: Osa Peninsula Corcovado Rainforest Expedition & Local Cuisine Experience
experiences.description: Venture into Corcovado National Park, dubbed by National Geographic as 'the most biologically intense place on Earth,' with a ranger-guided trek to encounter tapirs, peccaries, harpy eagles, and all four Costa Rican monkey species. End the day at a local 'soda' (family-run restaurant) in Puerto Jiménez savoring a traditional 'casado' plate of rice, beans, plantains, and fresh-caught fish, immersing yourself in authentic Costa Rican culture and cuisine.
experiences.location: Corcovado National Park, Osa Peninsula, Puntarenas Province

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Costa Rica
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Juan Santamaría International Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and arrange pre-booked shared shuttle or public bus to Aegean Bliss Resort (budget tip: shared shuttles cost ~$15–25 vs $80+ for private taxis). Check in, freshen up, and rest.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane or airport food court
meals.dinner: Grab a quick bite at the airport — Subway or local soda (small eatery) near arrivals for under $8

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange your airport transfer before arrival to save money and avoid stress at night. Keep colones (CRC) or USD on hand. February is dry season — expect warm, sunny weather. Store valuables securely upon arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After a leisurely wake-up, take a free orientation walk along the beachfront near Aegean Bliss Resort. Explore the local neighborhood, find the nearest supermarket or pulpería (corner store) to stock up on snacks and water for the days ahead.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the nearest public beach (Costa Rica beaches are free by law). Swim, snorkel if you brought gear, and watch for wildlife like pelicans, frigate birds, and hermit crabs along the shoreline. Many beachfront areas have free tide pools to explore.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll the local town center or boardwalk. Watch the sunset from the beach — one of Costa Rica's best free experiences. Explore local sodas (traditional Costa Rican diners) for an authentic and affordable dinner.

meals.breakfast: Casado breakfast at a local soda near the resort — eggs, gallo pinto, fruit, and coffee for ~$4–6
meals.lunch: Fresh coconut water and fruit from a beachside vendor (~$2–3) plus a quick bite at a local pulpería
meals.dinner: Dinner at a local soda — try arroz con pollo or casado for ~$5–8. Ask locals for their favorite spot.

day_by_day.notes: Day 2 is intentionally relaxed to recover from travel. Pick up a SIM card (Kölbi or Claro) at a local store for ~$10 with data to help navigate. Download maps offline. Stay hydrated in the tropical heat.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning wildlife walk along a local nature trail or mangrove estuary near the resort. Look for howler monkeys, scarlet macaws, iguanas, and coatis. Bring binoculars if possible. Many coastal areas have free or low-cost guided community walks (~$5–10).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby national park or wildlife refuge (entry fees typically $10–18 for foreigners). Explore marked trails through tropical dry forest or rainforest, spotting reptiles, birds, and mammals. Bring plenty of water and sunscreen.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area. Relax on the beach for golden hour. Head to a local restaurant for a budget seafood dinner — fresh catch of the day is often cheaper at local spots than tourist restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Gallo pinto with eggs and fresh tropical fruit at the resort or nearby soda (~$4–5)
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch from the supermarket — bread, local cheese, fruit, and juice (~$3–4 total)
meals.dinner: Fresh grilled fish at a local soda or beachside comedor — ~$7–10 including rice and salad

day_by_day.notes: Wear light, breathable clothing and closed-toe shoes for trail walks. Apply insect repellent before entering forested areas. February dry season means trails are generally dry and accessible. Carry a small daypack with essentials.

day_by_day.morning: Book a budget zip-lining experience through a local operator (shop around — prices range from $35–65 depending on location and number of cables). Many zip-line operators offer morning slots starting at 7:00–8:00 AM. Look for community-run or locally owned operators for better prices and authentic experiences.
day_by_day.afternoon: After zip-lining, visit a nearby waterfall or swimming hole — many are accessible via short hikes and are free or have a small entrance fee (~$2–5). Cool off in the natural pools and enjoy the jungle scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Tired from adventure — head back to the resort area. Cook a simple meal if your accommodation has a kitchen, or visit a local soda for a budget dinner. Share stories with fellow travelers at a hostel common area or beachside bar.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before zip-lining — banana, granola bar, and coffee from a local bakery (~$2–3)
meals.lunch: Many zip-line operators include a light snack; supplement with fruit and snacks from your daypack
meals.dinner: Rice and beans with chicken at a local soda (~$5–7). Try a fresh agua de pipa (coconut water) for dessert.

day_by_day.notes: Book zip-lining 1–2 days in advance through your hotel or a local tour desk to secure spots and possibly negotiate group rates. Wear closed-toe shoes and avoid loose jewelry. Most operators provide helmets and harnesses. Weight limits typically apply (check in advance).

day_by_day.morning: Take a budget day trip to a nearby wildlife sanctuary or rescue center (~$15–25 entry). These centers rehabilitate sloths, monkeys, toucans, and other injured animals. It's an educational and deeply rewarding wildlife experience. Many offer guided tours included in the entry fee.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a local farmers market or artisan market in the nearest town. Pick up fresh tropical fruits, local snacks, and handmade souvenirs at very low prices. Chat with vendors for an authentic cultural exchange.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset yoga or meditation on the beach (many budget hostels and community centers offer free or donation-based classes). Reflect on the day's wildlife encounters. Enjoy a quiet evening by the water.

meals.breakfast: Fresh fruit smoothie and toast at a local café (~$3–5)
meals.lunch: Street food at the farmers market — empanadas, chorreadas (corn pancakes), or tamales (~$2–4)
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal with market finds if you have kitchen access, or soda dinner for ~$6–8

day_by_day.notes: Choose reputable, ethical wildlife sanctuaries — look for ones affiliated with SINAC (Costa Rica's national conservation system) or internationally recognized rescue organizations. Avoid any facility that allows direct animal contact for photos, as this can indicate poor welfare standards.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning birdwatching walk — Costa Rica has over 900 bird species. Head to a nearby estuary, lagoon, or forested trail at dawn (5:30–7:00 AM) when birds are most active. Free if done independently; budget guided tours available for ~$15–20.
day_by_day.afternoon: Learn to surf or take a stand-up paddleboard (SUP) lesson on the beach. Many local surf schools offer budget group lessons for ~$25–35 including board rental. February dry season offers good wave conditions on Pacific beaches.
day_by_day.evening: Beach bonfire or stargazing — Costa Rica's dry season skies are incredibly clear. Find a quiet beach spot away from light pollution. Many budget hostels organize free communal evening activities.

meals.breakfast: Gallo pinto, eggs, and coffee — the classic Costa Rican breakfast at a soda (~$4)
meals.lunch: Beachside ceviche from a local vendor — fresh, cheap, and delicious (~$4–6)
meals.dinner: Casado plate at a local restaurant — rice, beans, salad, plantains, and protein (~$6–8)

day_by_day.notes: For birdwatching, download the free Merlin Bird ID app by Cornell Lab — it helps identify birds by sound and sight. Bring a small notebook to log sightings. Early morning and late afternoon are the best times for both birds and wildlife activity generally.

day_by_day.morning: Mid-trip rest and exploration day. Sleep in or enjoy a slow morning at the resort beachfront. Explore the local area on foot or rent a bicycle (~$5–10/day) to cover more ground and discover hidden spots nearby.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local waterfall hike or nature reserve within easy reach of the resort. Many lesser-known spots have little to no entrance fee and fewer crowds than major tourist sites. Ask locals or hostel staff for insider tips.
day_by_day.evening: Splurge slightly on a nicer dinner to celebrate the halfway point of your trip — look for a restaurant with fresh seafood and local ingredients. Even a 'nicer' local restaurant in Costa Rica can be very affordable (~$12–15 per person).

meals.breakfast: Treat yourself to a full breakfast at a café — fresh juice, gallo pinto, eggs, and fruit (~$6–8)
meals.lunch: Light lunch — sandwich or wrap from a local bakery (~$3–5)
meals.dinner: Mid-range local seafood restaurant — grilled mahi-mahi or sea bass with sides (~$12–15)

day_by_day.notes: Day 7 is intentionally lighter to prevent burnout on a 13-day trip. Use this day to do laundry, recharge devices, back up photos, and plan the remaining days. Check in with family or friends back home. Review your budget spending so far.

day_by_day.morning: Take a public bus or shared shuttle to a nearby national park or eco-reserve (~$5–15 transport, $10–18 entry). Spend the morning on a self-guided hike through primary or secondary rainforest, watching for monkeys, sloths, and exotic birds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the park or reserve — look for reptiles like basilisk lizards (the 'Jesus Christ lizard' that runs on water), poison dart frogs, and leaf-cutter ant colonies. These are free to observe and endlessly fascinating.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area by late afternoon. Rinse off and head out for a casual evening exploring the local nightlife scene — even on a budget, a cold Imperial beer (Costa Rica's national beer) at a local bar is only ~$1.50–2.50.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before the bus — granola, banana, and instant coffee prepared at the accommodation (~$1–2)
meals.lunch: Pack a lunch from the supermarket to eat in the park — saves money and time (~$3–5)
meals.dinner: Local soda near the resort — try olla de carne (beef and vegetable stew) or sopa negra (black bean soup) (~$5–7)

day_by_day.notes: Always check national park opening hours and whether advance reservations are required (some popular parks like Manuel Antonio require online booking). Carry your passport or a photocopy as ID. Wear neutral-colored clothing in the forest to avoid disturbing wildlife.

day_by_day.morning: Try a budget white-water rafting experience on a nearby river — Class II–III rapids are perfect for beginners and cost ~$45–65 with a local operator (often includes transport, equipment, and snacks). Book through a locally owned company for best prices.
day_by_day.afternoon: After rafting, visit a local hot spring if any are nearby — some community-run natural hot springs are free or very low cost (~$5–10) compared to resort-style ones ($50+). Soak tired muscles in mineral-rich thermal waters.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort. Light stretching or yoga on the beach. Enjoy a simple, nourishing dinner and early bedtime after an active day.

meals.breakfast: High-energy breakfast before rafting — eggs, toast, banana, and coffee at a local soda (~$4–5)
meals.lunch: Snack provided by rafting operator, or grab a quick roadside lunch on the way back (~$3–5)
meals.dinner: Comforting casado or pasta at a local restaurant (~$6–8). Treat yourself to a fresh fruit dessert.

day_by_day.notes: White-water rafting operators provide all safety equipment. Listen carefully to the safety briefing. Don't bring valuables on the raft — leave them in a locker or at the hotel. Secure your camera in a waterproof case if bringing one. Minimum age and weight requirements may apply.

day_by_day.morning: Explore a local fishing village or coastal community near the resort. Walk the docks in the early morning to watch fishermen bring in their catch. This is a wonderful cultural experience and completely free. Some fishermen may offer informal boat tours at very low cost.
day_by_day.afternoon: Snorkeling adventure — rent basic snorkel gear (~$5–10/day) and explore the reef or rocky outcrops near the beach. Costa Rica's Pacific coast has excellent marine biodiversity including sea turtles, rays, and tropical fish. Many spots are accessible directly from the beach.
day_by_day.evening: Cooking class or food experience — some local families and small operators offer budget cooking classes (~$20–30) teaching traditional Costa Rican dishes like gallo pinto, ceviche, and plantain dishes. A fantastic cultural and culinary experience.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and fresh pan dulce (sweet bread) from a local bakery (~$2–3)
meals.lunch: Fresh ceviche or grilled fish from a beachside shack — ultra-fresh and ultra-cheap (~$4–7)
meals.dinner: Eat what you cooked in the cooking class, or head to a local soda for a traditional dinner (~$5–8)

day_by_day.notes: When snorkeling, never touch coral or marine life. Apply reef-safe sunscreen only. Be aware of currents and always snorkel with a buddy. The cooking class dinner option is a great way to socialize with other travelers and locals alike.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day eco-adventure: book a guided canopy walk or hanging bridges tour through the forest (~$20–35 with a local operator). Unlike zip-lining, hanging bridges allow you to walk at canopy level and observe wildlife up close — sloths, toucans, and monkeys are commonly spotted.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local butterfly garden or frog exhibit (~$10–15) — compact, educational, and packed with incredible biodiversity. Many feature dozens of species of tropical butterflies, poison dart frogs, and other fascinating creatures in naturalistic enclosures.
day_by_day.evening: Night walk tour (~$15–25 with a local guide) — the rainforest at night is a completely different world. Spot nocturnal animals including kinkajous, night monkeys, sleeping birds, tarantulas, and glowing fungi. An unforgettable experience.

meals.breakfast: Hearty breakfast before the full day — gallo pinto, eggs, fruit, and coffee at a soda (~$5–6)
meals.lunch: Pack snacks and lunch for the canopy walk — fruit, nuts, sandwiches from the supermarket (~$3–4)
meals.dinner: Early dinner before the night walk — quick and filling casado at a local restaurant (~$6–8)

day_by_day.notes: Day 11 is your most activity-packed wildlife day — pace yourself. Wear long sleeves and pants for the night walk to protect against insects. Bring a small flashlight or headlamp (red light mode is best to avoid disturbing animals). Book the night walk in advance as spots fill up quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Free morning — revisit your favorite beach, trail, or viewpoint. Take time to journal, sketch, or simply absorb the natural beauty of Costa Rica. This is also a great time to shop for last-minute souvenirs at local markets — look for handmade crafts, coffee, and chocolate.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local coffee or cacao plantation if one is accessible from the resort area (~$15–25 for a tour). Learn about Costa Rica's world-famous coffee production, taste different roasts, and buy fresh beans to take home at local prices (much cheaper than airport shops).
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner — splurge slightly on your last full evening. Find a well-reviewed local restaurant (not a tourist trap) and enjoy a full Costa Rican meal with fresh seafood, local beer, and traditional desserts like tres leches cake or arroz con leche.

meals.breakfast: Slow breakfast at a café — fresh fruit bowl, yogurt, granola, and Costa Rican coffee (~$5–7)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the plantation or a nearby soda (~$4–6)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a quality local restaurant — budget ~$15–20 per person including a drink. A worthy splurge on your last night.

day_by_day.notes: Use today to pack, organize receipts, and ensure all souvenirs and purchases are within airline baggage limits. Vacuum-seal bags can help compress clothing. Declare any food items (like coffee or chocolate) at customs. Check your flight details and confirm your departure transfer.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Costa Rica — wake up for one last sunrise on the beach. Take a slow walk, breathe in the ocean air, and say goodbye to the wildlife and landscapes that made this trip unforgettable. Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort (confirm checkout time with hotel).
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight time, either head directly to the airport or enjoy a few final hours exploring the local area. Juan Santamaría Airport is in Alajuela — allow at least 3 hours before international departure. Take a shared shuttle or public bus to save on transport (~$15–25 vs $80+ taxi).
day_by_day.evening: Depart Costa Rica with incredible memories of zip-lining through the jungle, spotting sloths and scarlet macaws, surfing Pacific waves, and experiencing the pure life — Pura Vida! Safe travels home.

meals.breakfast: Final gallo pinto and coffee breakfast at a local soda near the resort (~$4–5) — savor it!
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the airport or grab a final empanada or sandwich before departing (~$5–8)
meals.dinner: On the plane or at your layover airport

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at Juan Santamaría Airport at least 3 hours before your international flight. Costa Rica charges a departure tax (usually included in your ticket now, but confirm). Use remaining colones on food or last-minute gifts at the airport — it's difficult to exchange them abroad. Remember: Pura Vida is not just a phrase, it's a way of life — carry it home with you!

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Juan Santamaría International Airport (SJO) at 22:30 on Flight UA. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and meet your pre-arranged private transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, unwind, and get a good night's rest.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight or airport snack
meals.lunch: N/A — in-flight meal
meals.dinner: Grab a light late-night snack at the resort's 24-hour front desk or room service if available — budget ~$10–15

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange your airport transfer in advance to avoid stress upon late arrival. Keep essentials like your passport, insurance, and resort confirmation easily accessible. Exchange a small amount of USD to Costa Rican Colones at the airport kiosk for tips and incidentals.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely resort breakfast. Take a slow orientation walk along the beachfront to get your bearings, breathe in the Pacific air, and acclimate to Costa Rica's tropical climate. Visit the resort's concierge to confirm upcoming tour bookings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local area surrounding Aegean Bliss Resort on foot or by bicycle rental. Visit a nearby nature trail or beach estuary to spot shorebirds, iguanas, and coastal wildlife — a gentle introduction to Costa Rica's incredible biodiversity without overexerting after travel.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed sunset on the beach, then head to a local beachside soda (traditional Costa Rican diner) for your first authentic Tico meal. Return to the resort early for a full night of rest before the adventures begin.

meals.breakfast: Resort buffet breakfast — budget ~$12–18 per person
meals.lunch: Casual beachside café near the resort — try a casado (rice, beans, protein, salad) for ~$8–12
meals.dinner: Local soda near the resort — try arroz con pollo or fresh ceviche — budget ~$10–15 per person

day_by_day.notes: This is a recovery and orientation day. Don't over-plan — jet lag is real. Use the afternoon to hydrate, apply sunscreen, and purchase any essentials at a nearby supermarket or pharmacy. Costa Rica's sun is intense year-round.

day_by_day.morning: Early departure by private shuttle toward the Arenal Volcano region (approximately 3–4 hours depending on resort location). Enjoy the scenic drive through Costa Rica's central highlands. Arrive and check in at a mid-range lodge near La Fortuna for a 2-night stay.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arenal Volcano Hanging Bridges & Hot Springs Evening (Part 1 — Afternoon): Begin the hanging bridges walk through the lush rainforest canopy surrounding Arenal Volcano. A certified naturalist guide will lead you across 16 bridges (6 suspension bridges), pointing out sloths, toucans, poison dart frogs, and howler monkeys in their natural habitat.
day_by_day.evening: Arenal Volcano Hanging Bridges & Hot Springs Evening (Part 2 — Evening): After the bridges walk, transition to the natural volcanic hot springs for a deeply relaxing evening soak under the stars. Many mid-range hot spring parks offer poolside service with tropical cocktails and light bites included.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure — budget ~$12–18
meals.lunch: Roadside soda or packed lunch during the shuttle journey — budget ~$8–12
meals.dinner: Dinner at the hot springs complex or a La Fortuna restaurant — try La Choza de Laurel for traditional Costa Rican cuisine — budget ~$15–22 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book the Arenal Hanging Bridges & Hot Springs combo tour in advance. Wear comfortable closed-toe shoes for the bridges walk and bring a swimsuit, towel, and a light change of clothes for the hot springs. Mosquito repellent is essential in this region.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for a guided wildlife walk around Lake Arenal at sunrise — one of the best times to spot birds and animals. Look for kingfishers, herons, caimans, and the iconic Jesus Christ lizard (basilisk) running across the water's surface.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore La Fortuna waterfall — a stunning 70-meter cascade set in lush jungle. Hike down the 500+ steps to the base for a refreshing swim in the natural pool. This is one of Costa Rica's most photogenic natural landmarks and very accessible from the area.
day_by_day.evening: Free evening in La Fortuna town. Browse the artisan market for handcrafted souvenirs, enjoy a locally roasted Costa Rican coffee at a café, and have dinner at a mid-range restaurant with views of the illuminated Arenal Volcano.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your La Fortuna lodge — budget ~$10–15
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch near La Fortuna waterfall or a café at the trailhead — budget ~$8–12
meals.dinner: Restaurante Nene's or similar local spot in La Fortuna — try the grilled tilapia or gallo pinto — budget ~$14–20 per person

day_by_day.notes: The La Fortuna waterfall hike is moderately strenuous on the return climb. Wear sturdy shoes and bring water. Entry fee is approximately $18 USD. The swim at the base is cold but incredibly refreshing. Avoid going after heavy rainfall as currents can be strong.

day_by_day.morning: Depart La Fortuna by private shuttle or shared jeep-boat-jeep transfer across Lake Arenal toward Monteverde — a scenic and adventurous 3-hour journey that is itself a highlight of any Costa Rica trip. Arrive in Monteverde and check in at a mid-range cloud forest lodge.
day_by_day.afternoon: After settling in, visit the Monteverde Butterfly Garden or the Hummingbird Gallery near the Santa Elena reserve — a gentle and visually stunning introduction to Monteverde's extraordinary biodiversity. Watch dozens of hummingbird species feed just inches from your face.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a guided night walk in the Santa Elena Cloud Forest Reserve. Nocturnal wildlife including glass frogs, red-eyed tree frogs, sleeping birds, tarantulas, and stick insects come alive after dark. This is a truly magical experience unique to Monteverde.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your La Fortuna lodge before departure — budget ~$10–15
meals.lunch: Café or soda in Santa Elena town upon arrival — try a typical Tico lunch plate — budget ~$8–12
meals.dinner: Sofía Restaurant or Taco Taco in Santa Elena — creative Costa Rican fusion cuisine — budget ~$15–22 per person

day_by_day.notes: The jeep-boat-jeep transfer across Lake Arenal is the most scenic and efficient route to Monteverde — book it through your resort concierge. Bring a light rain jacket as Monteverde is a cloud forest and mist and light rain are common year-round. The night walk requires a small group booking — reserve in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour: Experience one of Costa Rica's most iconic adventures — soaring through the misty cloud forest canopy on a thrilling zip-line circuit. With lines stretching up to 1.5 km and platforms perched high in the canopy, this is an adrenaline-fueled perspective of the cloud forest ecosystem like no other.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Monteverde Cloud Forest Biological Reserve for a self-guided or guided afternoon walk. This world-famous reserve protects over 100 mammal species, 400 bird species, and thousands of plant species. Keep your eyes peeled for the resplendent quetzal — one of the most sought-after bird sightings in all of Central America.
day_by_day.evening: Relax over dinner in Santa Elena and reflect on the day's adventures. Visit the local cheese factory shop (Monteverde is famous for its dairy) to pick up artisan cheeses and local chocolate for snacking.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at your lodge before the zip-line tour — budget ~$10–15
meals.lunch: Lunch at the zip-line operator's on-site café or a nearby soda — budget ~$8–14
meals.dinner: El Jardín Restaurant or Sabor Tico in Santa Elena — budget ~$14–20 per person

day_by_day.notes: The Monteverde zip-line tour typically lasts 3–4 hours including transportation and safety briefing. Weight limits apply (usually 120 kg/265 lbs max). Wear closed-toe shoes and clothes you don't mind getting dirty. The afternoon reserve walk is best done with a guide to maximize wildlife sightings — reserve slots fill quickly on weekends.

day_by_day.morning: Free morning in Monteverde — optional visit to the Orchid Garden (over 450 orchid species on display) or the Frog Pond, where you can observe 28 species of frogs in climate-controlled terrariums. A wonderful experience for wildlife enthusiasts of all ages.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart Monteverde by private shuttle heading south toward Manuel Antonio (approximately 4–5 hours). The drive takes you through the Central Valley and down to the Pacific coast. Arrive at a mid-range hotel near Manuel Antonio National Park and check in.
day_by_day.evening: First evening in Manuel Antonio — stroll along Biesanz Beach or Playa Espadilla for sunset, then explore the Quepos town waterfront. Quepos offers a vibrant mix of local sodas and international restaurants at mid-range prices.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your Monteverde lodge — budget ~$10–15
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or roadside soda stop during the drive — budget ~$8–12
meals.dinner: El Patio de Café Milagro in Quepos — creative Costa Rican cuisine with local ingredients — budget ~$16–24 per person

day_by_day.notes: The Monteverde to Manuel Antonio transfer is long — consider a shared shuttle to save costs (~$35–50 per person) versus a private transfer (~$150–200). Book in advance. Arrive in Quepos before dark to make the most of the evening. Manuel Antonio has a well-established tourist infrastructure with excellent mid-range dining options.

day_by_day.morning: Manuel Antonio National Park Guided Eco-Hike (Morning): Set out early with a certified naturalist guide to explore Costa Rica's most biodiverse national park before the midday heat and crowds. Your guide will help you spot white-faced capuchin monkeys, three-toed sloths, scarlet macaws, coatis, and the elusive Manuel Antonio squirrel monkey — found nowhere else on Earth.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the guided hike, spend the afternoon relaxing on the pristine white-sand beaches inside the park — Playa Manuel Antonio is widely considered one of the most beautiful beaches in Costa Rica. Swim, snorkel, or simply enjoy the remarkable experience of sharing the beach with monkeys and iguanas.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Quepos or your hotel area for a sunset cocktail at a cliffside bar overlooking the Pacific, followed by dinner at one of Manuel Antonio's excellent mid-range restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at your hotel before the park opening — budget ~$10–15
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch inside the park (bring your own — no food vendors inside) — budget ~$8–12 for pre-purchased items
meals.dinner: La Luna Restaurant or Agua Azul — fresh seafood with ocean views — budget ~$18–28 per person

day_by_day.notes: Manuel Antonio National Park has a daily visitor cap — book your guided eco-hike and park entry tickets well in advance, especially for February (peak season). The park is closed on Tuesdays. Enter as early as possible (7:00 AM) for the best wildlife sightings. Do not feed the animals — it is illegal and harmful to their health.

day_by_day.morning: Manuel Antonio National Park is closed on Tuesdays — perfect day for a kayaking or snorkeling tour in the calm waters around Biesanz Beach. A guided sea kayaking excursion offers a unique marine perspective of the park's coastline and a chance to spot marine wildlife including dolphins, sea turtles, and tropical fish.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Titi Conservation Alliance or a local wildlife rescue center near Manuel Antonio — a meaningful experience where you can learn about Costa Rica's conservation efforts and see rescued sloths, monkeys, and birds up close in a responsible, ethical setting.
day_by_day.evening: Cooking class or cultural experience in Quepos — several local operators offer hands-on Costa Rican cooking classes where you'll learn to prepare traditional dishes like gallo pinto, ceviche, and tres leches cake using locally sourced ingredients.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your hotel — budget ~$10–15
meals.lunch: Beachside café in the Manuel Antonio area — fresh ceviche and patacones — budget ~$10–15
meals.dinner: Dinner from your cooking class experience or a local soda in Quepos — budget ~$12–18 per person

day_by_day.notes: Tuesday is the ideal day to explore alternatives since the national park is closed. Book the kayaking tour and cooking class in advance. The wildlife rescue center visit is a responsible wildlife experience — look for centers accredited by the Costa Rican government (SINAC) to ensure ethical standards.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Manuel Antonio by domestic flight or private shuttle toward Drake Bay / Puerto Jiménez on the Osa Peninsula (approximately 5–6 hours by road or 45 minutes by small aircraft). Domestic flights from Quepos to Drake Bay are affordable and spectacular. Check in at a mid-range eco-lodge in the Osa Peninsula.
day_by_day.afternoon: Osa Peninsula Corcovado Rainforest Expedition (Orientation Afternoon): After arriving, meet your expedition guide for a briefing on tomorrow's full Corcovado day. Take an introductory walk around the lodge's private trails to begin spotting wildlife — scarlet macaws, white-lipped peccaries, and tapir tracks are commonly found right at the lodge perimeter.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a communal dinner at your eco-lodge — many Osa lodges offer family-style meals featuring locally caught fish, tropical fruits, and organic vegetables grown on-site. The Osa Peninsula has virtually no light pollution — spend the evening stargazing from the lodge deck.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your Manuel Antonio hotel before departure — budget ~$10–15
meals.lunch: In-flight snack or lunch at Puerto Jiménez upon arrival — try a local soda for fresh fish — budget ~$8–14
meals.dinner: Eco-lodge communal dinner — typically included or ~$20–30 per person with fresh local ingredients

day_by_day.notes: The Osa Peninsula is remote — ATMs are scarce and internet is limited. Bring sufficient cash (USD or Colones), a power bank, and all necessary medications. Domestic flights from Quepos/Quepos Airport (XQP) to Drake Bay (DRK) operate on small 12-seat Cessna aircraft — weight limits apply (usually 12 kg/26 lbs per person including carry-on). Book well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Osa Peninsula Corcovado Rainforest Expedition (Full Day): Depart at dawn with your expert naturalist guide into Corcovado National Park — dubbed by National Geographic as 'the most biologically intense place on Earth.' Trek through primary rainforest teeming with wildlife: Baird's tapirs, giant anteaters, four species of monkeys, harpy eagles, and an astonishing array of reptiles and amphibians.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Corcovado expedition deep into the park's interior. Enjoy a packed lunch beside a jungle river or waterfall. Your guide will share knowledge about the park's extraordinary ecosystem, medicinal plants, and the conservation challenges facing this irreplaceable habitat.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the eco-lodge by late afternoon, thoroughly exhilarated and humbled by the day's wildlife encounters. Enjoy a traditional Costa Rican dinner experience paired with local cuisine — your guide may share stories of the park over the meal.

meals.breakfast: Early pre-dawn breakfast at the eco-lodge before departure — typically included
meals.lunch: Packed jungle lunch provided by the tour operator — typically included in the Corcovado expedition package
meals.dinner: Eco-lodge dinner featuring local Osa Peninsula cuisine — budget ~$20–30 or included in lodge package

day_by_day.notes: The Corcovado expedition is physically demanding — expect 8–10 hours of hiking on uneven terrain in heat and humidity. Wear moisture-wicking clothing, sturdy waterproof hiking boots, and bring plenty of water (minimum 3 liters). The local cuisine experience is integrated into the expedition — your guide will introduce you to traditional Osa dishes and possibly a local farming family.

day_by_day.morning: Morning boat safari or dolphin-watching tour in the Golfo Dulce — the warm, sheltered gulf surrounding the Osa Peninsula is home to resident spinner and bottlenose dolphins, humpback whales (seasonal), sea turtles, and bull sharks. A guided boat tour offers a stunning marine counterpart to the previous day's jungle adventure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to San José by domestic flight from Puerto Jiménez or Drake Bay to Juan Santamaría International Airport. Check in at a mid-range hotel near the airport or in the Escazú / Santa Ana district for a comfortable final night before your departure.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in San José — explore the Barrio Amón historic district, visit the Pre-Columbian Gold Museum (open until 5 PM), or enjoy a farewell dinner at a top-rated San José restaurant. Celebrate 12 incredible days in Costa Rica with a proper Tico feast.

meals.breakfast: Final eco-lodge breakfast on the Osa Peninsula — typically included
meals.lunch: Light lunch in Puerto Jiménez before your flight — local soda near the airstrip — budget ~$8–12
meals.dinner: Nuestra Tierra or Machu Picchu Restaurant in San José — authentic Costa Rican and Peruvian fusion — budget ~$18–28 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book your domestic return flight from Osa to San José well in advance — these small-aircraft routes fill up quickly during peak season. Confirm your international departure flight details and ensure you arrive at SJO at least 3 hours before departure. Pack your souvenirs, artisan goods, and locally roasted coffee carefully.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Costa Rica — if your flight departs in the afternoon or evening, use the morning for last-minute souvenir shopping at the Mercado Central in San José or the artisan market in Escazú. Pick up locally produced coffee, chocolate, hot sauce, and handcrafted jewelry as gifts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Juan Santamaría International Airport (SJO) with plenty of time to spare. Complete check-in, clear security, and enjoy a final cup of Costa Rican coffee at an airport café before boarding. Reflect on 13 days of extraordinary eco-adventure, zip-lining through cloud forests, and wildlife encounters that will last a lifetime.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Costa Rica — Pura Vida!

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your San José hotel — budget ~$10–15
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the Mercado Central or airport restaurant — budget ~$10–15
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport dining before departure

day_by_day.notes: Costa Rica charges a departure tax — confirm whether it is included in your airline ticket or must be paid separately at the airport ($29 USD if not included). Allow extra time for SJO airport security during peak February travel season. Declare any agricultural products (coffee beans in sealed packaging is generally fine) at customs. Say 'Pura Vida' one last time — you've earned it!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Costa Rica Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour
experiences.description: Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most thrilling zip-line circuits, featuring over 10 cables, Tarzan swings, and suspension bridges. Spot howler monkeys, toucans, and resplendent quetzals from a bird's-eye view while gliding above the treetops at speeds up to 50 mph.

experiences.name: Tortuguero National Park Wildlife Boat Safari
experiences.description: Glide through the jungle canals of Tortuguero on a guided boat safari teeming with wildlife. Observe caimans, river turtles, three-toed sloths, poison dart frogs, and over 300 bird species in their natural habitat. If visiting between July and October, witness the awe-inspiring nesting of endangered green sea turtles on the beach at night.

experiences.name: Manuel Antonio National Park Guided Eco-Hike
experiences.description: Explore Costa Rica's most biodiverse national park with a certified naturalist guide who will help you spot white-faced capuchin monkeys, two-toed sloths, scarlet macaws, and the rare squirrel monkey. The hike winds through lush rainforest trails that open onto stunning white-sand beaches, offering a perfect blend of wildlife and natural beauty.

experiences.name: Arenal Volcano Hanging Bridges & Hot Springs Evening
experiences.description: Walk among the rainforest canopy on a series of hanging bridges near the iconic Arenal Volcano, spotting poison dart frogs, leaf-cutter ants, and exotic birds. Cap the adventure with a relaxing soak in natural volcanic hot springs surrounded by lush jungle, a perfect recovery after days of eco-adventure activities.
experiences.location: La Fortuna de San Carlos, Alajuela Province

experiences.name: Osa Peninsula Corcovado Rainforest Expedition & Local Cuisine Experience
experiences.description: Venture into Corcovado National Park, dubbed by National Geographic as 'the most biologically intense place on Earth,' with a ranger-guided trek to encounter tapirs, peccaries, harpy eagles, and all four Costa Rican monkey species. End the day at a local 'soda' (family-run restaurant) in Puerto Jiménez savoring a traditional 'casado' plate of rice, beans, plantains, and fresh-caught fish, immersing yourself in authentic Costa Rican culture and cuisine.
experiences.location: Corcovado National Park, Osa Peninsula, Puntarenas Province

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Juan Santamaría International Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. A private luxury transfer with a bilingual chauffeur will greet you at arrivals with a personalized welcome sign. Enjoy chilled towels, bottled water, and light snacks in the vehicle during the scenic transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in to your beachfront suite and unwind with a complimentary welcome cocktail prepared by the resort's in-room butler service.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable
meals.lunch: Not applicable
meals.dinner: Late-night in-room dining from the resort's 24-hour premium menu — recommended: fresh ceviche, tropical fruit platter, and a glass of Costa Rican craft beer or local guaro sour

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange express check-in with the resort concierge before departure to minimize wait time upon late arrival. Request turndown service and a morning wake-up call setup. Confirm all luggage is accounted for before leaving the airport.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely beachfront breakfast at the resort. After breakfast, take a private guided orientation walk of the resort grounds and surrounding coastal area with the resort naturalist, spotting local bird species, coastal flora, and learning about the region's ecology. Settle into your suite and arrange the week's itinerary with the dedicated concierge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at the resort's infinity pool overlooking the Pacific, or opt for a private snorkeling excursion along the reef just off the beachfront. Enjoy a curated beach picnic lunch prepared by the resort chef with fresh local ingredients. In the mid-afternoon, indulge in a 90-minute couples' or solo oceanfront massage at the resort spa featuring volcanic stone therapy and local botanical oils.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the private beach terrace with the resort's mixologist crafting bespoke tropical drinks. Dinner at the resort's signature fine-dining restaurant featuring Costa Rican fusion cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Full à la carte breakfast at the resort's beachfront restaurant — recommended: gallo pinto with free-range eggs, fresh tropical fruit, Costa Rican Tarrazú coffee
meals.lunch: Private beach picnic curated by the resort chef — fresh lobster rolls, chilled gazpacho, local cheeses, and sparkling water
meals.dinner: Resort signature restaurant — recommended: sea bass in plantain crust with hearts of palm salad, followed by tres leches with passion fruit coulis; pair with a Costa Rican Sauvignon Blanc

day_by_day.notes: This is a deliberate recovery and orientation day after the late arrival. Use this time to acclimatize to the tropical climate, hydrate well, and finalize logistics for upcoming excursions with the concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning private wildlife walk along the resort's coastal trail and nearby mangrove area with a certified naturalist guide. Look for scarlet macaws, white-faced capuchin monkeys, coatis, and a variety of tropical birds at dawn when wildlife is most active. Return for a hearty breakfast at the resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart by private luxury 4x4 vehicle for Manuel Antonio National Park (approximately 30–45 minutes depending on resort location). Begin the Manuel Antonio National Park Guided Eco-Hike with a certified naturalist who will help you spot three-toed sloths, poison dart frogs, white-tipped deer, and hundreds of bird species. Explore the park's pristine trails leading to secluded beaches within the park boundaries.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by late afternoon. Freshen up and head to a nearby acclaimed local restaurant in the Manuel Antonio area for dinner, or dine at the resort with a special chef's tasting menu arranged in advance.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — açaí bowls, fresh-pressed tropical juices, eggs Benedict with smoked local fish
meals.lunch: Gourmet packed lunch provided by the resort or a stop at La Luna Restaurant (if near Manuel Antonio area) — known for its open-air terrace, fresh seafood, and organic local produce
meals.dinner: El Avión Restaurant, Manuel Antonio — a celebrated restaurant built inside a retired 1954 Fairchild C-123 cargo plane; recommended: shrimp in coconut curry, grilled mahi-mahi, and local craft beer

day_by_day.notes: Manuel Antonio National Park has a daily visitor cap — ensure park entry tickets are pre-booked by the concierge well in advance. Wear lightweight moisture-wicking clothing, apply reef-safe sunscreen, and bring binoculars for the best wildlife viewing experience.

day_by_day.morning: Early departure by private charter flight or luxury vehicle transfer toward the Osa Peninsula (approximately 1 hour by light aircraft or 4–5 hours by road — charter flight strongly recommended for premium experience). Arrive at a luxury eco-lodge base near Corcovado for the day's expedition. Begin the Osa Peninsula Corcovado Rainforest Expedition with expert naturalist guides into Corcovado National Park — dubbed by National Geographic as 'the most biologically intense place on Earth.'
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue deep into Corcovado, trekking through primary rainforest in search of jaguars, tapirs, giant anteaters, harpy eagles, and four species of monkeys. After the trek, participate in a curated Local Cuisine Experience hosted by a local Osa family — learn to prepare traditional dishes using ingredients foraged and grown in the rainforest buffer zone, including heart of palm stew, plantain dishes, and cacao-based desserts.
day_by_day.evening: Return transfer to the resort via private charter flight or vehicle. Arrive back at Aegean Bliss Resort for a relaxing evening. Optional: reserve the resort's private jacuzzi terrace for a stargazing session with a complimentary bottle of champagne.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the resort before departure — fresh fruit, granola, yogurt, and coffee
meals.lunch: Included as part of the Corcovado Local Cuisine Experience — traditional Osa-style lunch with rice, beans, fresh fish, tropical fruits, and homemade tortillas
meals.dinner: In-room private dining at the resort — chef's special of grilled local beef tenderloin with yuca purée, roasted vegetables, and a fine Malbec

day_by_day.notes: Corcovado National Park requires advance permits and a licensed guide — ensure the concierge arranges all paperwork. Wear sturdy waterproof hiking boots, long trousers for jungle protection, and carry insect repellent. This is one of the most demanding days physically — pace yourself and stay hydrated.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning at the resort after the Corcovado expedition. Enjoy a slow breakfast followed by a private yoga session on the beachfront deck with the resort's resident instructor at sunrise. Alternatively, take a kayaking or stand-up paddleboarding session in the calm waters in front of the resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private sport fishing charter departs from the nearest marina — spend the afternoon deep-sea fishing in the Pacific waters for marlin, sailfish, or dorado (catch-and-release encouraged). The luxury charter includes an onboard chef who prepares fresh ceviche and snacks from the catch. Return to the marina by late afternoon with a sunset backdrop.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner cocktails on the resort's beachfront fire pit. Special beachfront dinner under the stars arranged by the resort — a private table set on the sand with tiki torches, a personalized menu, and live acoustic guitar.

meals.breakfast: Smoothie bowls, avocado toast on artisan bread, fresh Costa Rican coffee at the resort
meals.lunch: Onboard the fishing charter — fresh ceviche, tropical fruit, cold-pressed juices, and light bites prepared by the boat's chef
meals.dinner: Private beachfront dinner at the resort — five-course tasting menu featuring local lobster, wagyu beef, tropical desserts; sommelier-selected wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: The private sport fishing charter must be booked in advance through the concierge. Confirm marine weather conditions the evening prior. Bring polarized sunglasses and reef-safe sunscreen for the full day on the water.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early by private luxury transfer toward Tortuguero on the Caribbean coast (a combination of road and private boat transfer, or light aircraft charter for premium speed and comfort). Arrive at a luxury eco-lodge base near Tortuguero. Begin the Tortuguero National Park Wildlife Boat Safari — glide through the jungle canal network in a private motor canoe with a certified naturalist guide. Spot river otters, green iguanas, caimans, river turtles, manatees, and an extraordinary array of tropical birds including toucans, herons, and kingfishers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the canal safari deeper into the park's remote waterways for a more exclusive, crowd-free wildlife experience. Stop at a secluded riverbank for a gourmet picnic lunch. In the afternoon, visit the Sea Turtle Conservancy visitor center to learn about Tortuguero's legendary sea turtle nesting programs (February is early in the green turtle season — a naturalist will advise on likelihood of sightings).
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort via private transfer. Enjoy a relaxing evening with a therapeutic soak in the resort's outdoor hot tub followed by a farm-to-table dinner highlighting Caribbean coastal flavors.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure — traditional gallo pinto, fresh fruit, and strong Costa Rican coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic on the riverbank during the boat safari — smoked fish, tropical fruits, local cheeses, fresh bread, and sparkling water
meals.dinner: Resort dinner with Caribbean-inspired menu — jerk-spiced snapper, coconut rice, fried plantains, and rum-infused crème brûlée

day_by_day.notes: Tortuguero is one of the most important sea turtle nesting sites in the world. February is transitional for nesting — confirm turtle activity with the naturalist upon arrival. The canals are best explored at dawn or dusk for maximum wildlife activity. Bring waterproof camera equipment.

day_by_day.morning: Mid-trip free day for rest, reflection, and resort indulgence. Begin with a sunrise meditation session on the beach. Follow with a full spa morning — choose from a menu of premium treatments including a volcanic mud wrap, deep tissue massage, or a traditional Temascal (pre-Columbian steam ceremony) experience if offered by the resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private horseback riding excursion along the beach and through nearby coastal trails with a local guide. The trail winds through secondary forest where you may spot howler monkeys and tropical birds. Return to the resort for afternoon tea on the veranda.
day_by_day.evening: Arrange a private cooking class with the resort's executive chef — learn to prepare three signature Costa Rican dishes using local, sustainably sourced ingredients. Dine on your creations in the resort's private dining room with a curated wine selection.

meals.breakfast: Champagne brunch at the resort — eggs any style, smoked salmon, fresh pastries, tropical fruit, mimosas
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch — grilled vegetable wraps, fresh fruit smoothies, and sparkling water
meals.dinner: Your own creations from the private cooking class, enjoyed in the resort's exclusive private dining room with sommelier-paired wines

day_by_day.notes: This is the halfway point of the trip — an intentional rest day to recharge before the second half of the itinerary. Encourage guests to journal, photograph, and reflect on wildlife encounters. Concierge should confirm all upcoming bookings and transfers today.

day_by_day.morning: Depart by private luxury vehicle toward the Arenal Volcano region (approximately 3–4 hours from the Pacific coast, or 1 hour by charter flight). Arrive at a premium lodge near Arenal with iconic volcano views. Begin the Arenal Volcano Hanging Bridges experience — walk among the rainforest canopy on a series of suspension bridges at varying heights, offering extraordinary perspectives of the rainforest ecosystem and views of the smoking Arenal Volcano. A private naturalist guide accompanies the walk to identify wildlife including toucans, morpho butterflies, and howler monkeys.
day_by_day.afternoon: Guided hike on the Arenal lava fields trail with a volcanologist or senior naturalist guide, exploring the 1968 lava flow zone and learning about the volcano's dramatic geological history. Return to the lodge for an afternoon of leisure by the volcano-view infinity pool.
day_by_day.evening: The signature experience of the day — an exclusive Hot Springs Evening at a premium private thermal pool complex (such as Tabacón Grand Spa Thermal Resort or equivalent). Soak in mineral-rich geothermal pools of varying temperatures surrounded by lush tropical gardens, with the illuminated volcano as a backdrop. Enjoy cocktails served poolside.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure — or a stop at a local café en route to Arenal
meals.lunch: Arenal lodge restaurant with volcano views — recommended: casado with local river fish, fresh salad, and natural fruit water
meals.dinner: Fine dining at the hot springs resort or the Arenal lodge's signature restaurant — recommended: slow-braised local beef, yuca gnocchi, and a Costa Rican chocolate lava cake for dessert

day_by_day.notes: Confirm hot springs reservation in advance as premium slots book quickly. The hanging bridges are best in the morning when wildlife is most active and mist is dramatic. Pack a light rain jacket as the Arenal microclimate can bring afternoon showers.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning birdwatching walk around the Arenal Lake and wetlands area with a specialist birding guide — the region is home to over 850 bird species including the resplendent quetzal in higher elevations. Spot roseate spoonbills, boat-billed herons, and numerous hummingbird species. Return to the lodge for breakfast with panoramic volcano views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private white-water rafting experience on the Sarapiquí or Balsa River (Class III–IV rapids, suitable for adventurous guests) with a certified safety guide and luxury support team. Alternatively, for a more relaxed option, enjoy a private kayaking tour on Lake Arenal with stunning volcano reflections. Post-activity, visit a local sustainable chocolate farm for a premium cacao tasting and tour.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Arenal lodge for a sunset cocktail hour on the volcano-view terrace. Private stargazing session with a telescope and a local astronomer guide — the Arenal region's low light pollution makes for exceptional night sky viewing.

meals.breakfast: Lodge breakfast with volcano views — fresh tropical fruits, traditional casado breakfast, Costa Rican specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Riverside picnic following the rafting experience — prepared by the lodge with sandwiches, fresh fruit, and cold drinks
meals.dinner: Lodge farm-to-table dinner featuring produce from the on-site organic garden — recommended: hearts of palm soup, grilled tilapia with chimichurri, and a local artisan cheese board

day_by_day.notes: Confirm river conditions and water levels with the rafting operator the evening prior — February is generally dry season which can affect rapids. The chocolate farm tour is a highlight for food enthusiasts and should be pre-booked.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Arenal by private vehicle toward Monteverde Cloud Forest (approximately 3-hour scenic drive, including the famous lake crossing by boat and 4x4 jeep — a classic Costa Rican adventure transfer). Arrive at a premium cloud forest lodge. After settling in, begin the Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour — soar through the misty cloud forest on one of Costa Rica's most thrilling zip-line circuits, featuring multiple lines including a Superman-style horizontal line and a Tarzan swing, with breathtaking views of the forest canopy and Pacific coast on clear days.
day_by_day.afternoon: Post-zip-line, visit the Monteverde Cloud Forest Biological Reserve for a private guided walk through the primary cloud forest — search for the legendary resplendent quetzal, three-wattled bellbirds, and golden-browed chlorophonias. The naturalist guide will explain the extraordinary epiphyte-rich ecosystem unique to cloud forests.
day_by_day.evening: Night walk in the cloud forest with a specialized nocturnal wildlife guide — spot sleeping birds, glass frogs, red-eyed tree frogs, stick insects, and tarantulas in their natural habitat using specialized torches.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the Arenal lodge before departure — or packed breakfast for the road
meals.lunch: Monteverde lodge restaurant — recommended: vegetable soup, local trout with cloud forest herbs, fresh lemonade
meals.dinner: Sofía Restaurant, Monteverde (or equivalent premium local option) — celebrated for its Nueva Latino cuisine; recommended: plantain-crusted chicken, local mushroom risotto, and tropical fruit sorbet

day_by_day.notes: The Jeep-Boat-Jeep transfer from Arenal to Monteverde is an iconic Costa Rica experience and far more scenic than the road route — confirm this transfer is arranged. Monteverde is cooler and misty — pack a light fleece or jacket. The night walk requires advance reservation with the reserve.

day_by_day.morning: Dawn birdwatching session at the cloud forest reserve — the best time to spot the resplendent quetzal (February is within quetzal nesting season, increasing sighting probability). A specialist quetzal guide will lead the search through the reserve's primary forest trails. Return to the lodge for a full breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Monteverde Butterfly Garden and Hummingbird Gallery for a private guided tour — walk through enclosed gardens with hundreds of butterfly species and stand among dozens of hummingbird feeders attracting rare species. Afternoon visit to a local artisan cheese factory (Monteverde is famous for its Swiss-influenced cheese-making tradition) for a premium tasting. Explore the charming Santa Elena village for local art, crafts, and souvenir shopping.
day_by_day.evening: Private transfer back toward the Pacific coast resort (approximately 3–4 hours) or overnight at the Monteverde lodge with an early departure the next morning. If returning, enjoy a welcome-back dinner at the resort.

meals.breakfast: Cloud forest lodge breakfast — homemade granola, local cheeses, fresh bread, and specialty Monteverde coffee
meals.lunch: Cheese factory tasting lunch — artisan cheeses, local bread, fruit preserves, and wine pairings
meals.dinner: If returning to resort: beachfront dinner at the resort with a celebratory menu; if staying in Monteverde: Tree House Restaurant (El Sapo Dorado) — renowned for its romantic cloud forest setting and excellent local cuisine

day_by_day.notes: Confirm quetzal guide booking in advance — these specialist guides are in high demand during nesting season. The cheese factory visit should be pre-arranged for a private premium tasting experience rather than a standard group tour.

day_by_day.morning: Final full day — return to Aegean Bliss Resort if not already back. Morning at leisure: enjoy one final sunrise walk on the beach, a private surf lesson with a certified instructor, or a snorkeling excursion to a nearby reef. Alternatively, arrange a private catamaran sailing tour along the Pacific coastline with snorkeling stops, dolphin watching, and a champagne sunset (if timing allows for an afternoon departure).
day_by_day.afternoon: Private catamaran sailing tour along the Pacific coast — snorkel in crystal-clear waters, watch for spinner dolphins and humpback whales (February is within whale migration season), and enjoy a gourmet lunch onboard with fresh ceviche, tropical fruits, and cold drinks. Return to the marina by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at the resort's finest venue — a special chef's table experience in the resort kitchen or a private candlelit dinner on the beach. The resort team arranges a personalized farewell with a photo book of the trip's highlights (pre-arranged with the concierge). Toast to the journey with a premium bottle of champagne.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell breakfast at the resort — full spread including all Costa Rican favorites, fresh juices, and specialty coffees
meals.lunch: Gourmet onboard the catamaran — fresh ceviche, tropical fruit platter, local cheeses, and chilled white wine
meals.dinner: Chef's table farewell dinner at the resort — seven-course tasting menu celebrating the best flavors of Costa Rica; sommelier-selected wine pairings for each course

day_by_day.notes: February is peak humpback whale migration season — confirm with the catamaran captain for best whale-watching zones. Request the concierge to prepare a curated gift bag of local products (artisan coffee, chocolate, hot sauce) as a farewell memento. Begin packing and confirm departure logistics tonight.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at leisure — enjoy a last sunrise on the beach, a quiet breakfast, and time to soak in the surroundings. Resort spa offers a pre-departure 'refresh' treatment (express massage or facial) to prepare for the journey home. Complete packing and checkout formalities with the resort concierge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer departs from the resort to Juan Santamaría International Airport in San José. The bilingual chauffeur assists with all luggage. Enjoy refreshments and snacks in the vehicle during the transfer. Arrive at the airport with ample time for premium check-in and lounge access.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Costa Rica. The concierge team will have arranged fast-track airport services, lounge access, and any necessary departure documentation. Carry memories of 13 extraordinary days of eco-adventure, wildlife, and luxury in one of the world's most biodiverse destinations.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — light and refreshing; fresh tropical fruit, yogurt, Costa Rican coffee, and pastries
meals.lunch: Premium airport lounge dining or a final stop at a quality San José restaurant near the airport if time permits — recommended: La Criollita for traditional Costa Rican cuisine
meals.dinner: In-flight dining or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before departure for international check-in, security, and immigration. Confirm all luggage weight limits, especially if purchasing local artisan goods or coffee. Ensure all wildlife souvenirs comply with CITES regulations — no animal products or live plants may be exported. Request the hotel to store luggage during the final morning if checkout is before the transfer.
